headline: Data-center crackdown fears and Qualcomm/Arm misses sink chips 12%; S&P 500 −4.4%
summary: The post-election rally unravelled within the first hour: the Dow briefly held gains at the open, but selling in chip and data-center stocks accelerated through the morning and the S&P 500 posted its worst day since April 2025, more than erasing Wednesday's jump. Losses were broad, with all 11 S&P sectors lower, technology down about 7.3% and consumer staples holding up best at about −0.7%, on heavy volume of about 26.9 billion shares versus a 17.7 billion average. The Nasdaq Composite and Nasdaq-100 closed in correction, and Treasuries caught a haven bid.
drivers: AI buildout fears turn into a chip rout

Investors priced the risk that a Democratic Congress and new state officials in data-center states could pause or regulate new construction, which would cut demand for AI chips and power gear. The SOX fell 12.25%, its worst day since March 2020; Nvidia (about −9%) was the heaviest drag on the S&P 500, AMD sank about 17%, Micron about 17%, and Broadcom and TSMC fell 9% or more.
Qualcomm and Arm results add fuel

Qualcomm fell about 9.5% after handset chip sales dropped 26% and its next-quarter profit outlook came in light, with a warning on rising supply-chain costs; Arm slid about 11% as guidance failed to impress. Memory and storage names (SanDisk, Western Digital, Seagate) posted steep double-digit losses.
Selling spreads to Big Tech and the wider AI trade

Meta lost 4% and Amazon and Alphabet about 2.2% each after Wednesday's rally; data-center and power names fell hard, with IREN and Applied Digital down more than 14%, CoreWeave nearly 10% and GE Vernova 7.5%, while Tesla and SpaceX dropped 9% or more. The S&P 500 shed about $3 trillion in value; AppLovin (+31%) and Tapestry (+7%) rose on strong results.
Haven bid in bonds; oil rebounds

The VIX jumped about 70% to 28.18, its highest close since late March, and the 10-year yield slipped about 5bp to 4.84% while the 2-year fell more on safety buying; Fed's Hammack and Barkin still hinted at possible hikes. WTI bounced 2.7% to $90.52 after Wednesday's 8% plunge as Middle East supply risk lingered; jobless claims (189K) and Q3 productivity (+3.6%) were firm.
week: Four sessions in, the S&P 500 is down about 3% and the Nasdaq about 4.4% for the week, the Dow nearly flat and the Russell 2000 down about 3%, with the Nasdaq and SOX now in correction (SOX about 38% below its June record); the backdrop is a hawkish-leaning Fed with a December hike still in play and crude far below last week's highs.
watch: Next: the October jobs report on Friday, Nov 6 is the key test for December Fed pricing; Cloudflare jumped about 18% after hours on its results, and any further statements on state data-center moratoriums will steer the chip names.
